{{Quote|Every day more bounty hunters are searching for me. I'm going to pay off Jabba before he sends any more of his remotes, Gank killers, and who knows what else. I've got to get this price off my head while I still have a head.|Han Solo explains his departure from [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] to Leia Organa|<ref name="ESBN">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref>}}
'''Ganks''', also known as '''Gank killers''',<ref name="ESBN" /> were a [[Blood/Legends|bloodthirsty]], bipedal [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. Members of the species usually wore high-tech battle [[Armor/Legends|armor]] from head to [[Limb/Legends|foot]], so to most non-Ganks their physical appearance remained unknown. Under the armor Ganks were [[Hair/Legends|hairy]] and powerful, with [[Color/Legends|yellow]], squarish faces and beady [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. They sported [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] [[Gank comm implant|implants]] that allowed them to communicate with one another silently. Ganks were rarely seen alone, as they moved around in packs and worked together to accomplish their aims. They relished opportunities for violent mayhem and [[Death/Legends|massacring]] others, a joy that only embellished their reputation as bloodthirsty killers.

Among the many mysteries surrounding the Ganks was the name of their true [[Gank homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], since most members of the species resided on the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]-controlled industrial [[Moon/Legends|moon]] known as [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. There they often were found working for Hutts&mdash;acting as [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]], and [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]]. They were infamous throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for their role in the [[Gank Massacres]], when they were hired by [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] to protect them from the ravages of the [[Porporite]] species, who were intent on gaining access to [[Ryll/Legends|ryll]] [[Spice/Legends|spice]]. The Ganks [[Speciecide|wiped out]] the Porporites and then mounted a full-scale campaign of conquest against neighboring groups until stopped by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|I'll pass on attackin' a Jedi. Ain't ya got some easier job that needs doin', like takin' on a hundred Gank Killers?|Finhead Stonebone rejects Bogga the Hutt's suggestion that he kill Jedi Master [[Thon]]|<ref name="TOTJ 4">[[Tales of the Jedi 4|''Tales of the Jedi'' 4]]</ref>}}
The Ganks were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Hair/Legends|fur]]-covered [[Diet/Legends|carnivores]]. The typical member of the species had a face that was squared-off and yellow in [[Color/Legends|color]], the expression trapped in a perpetual snarl<ref name="EGAS " /> that non-Ganks found unattractive.<ref name="EA">''[[Galaxy of Fear: Eaten Alive]]''</ref> Small, mean-looking [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]'' peered from above the [[Mouth/Legends|maw]],<ref name="EGAS " /> and [[Ear/Legends|ears]]'' facilitated the sense of hearing.<ref name="EA" /> The head sat atop a thick neck, which emerged from between broad, strong shoulders. These capped two thickset, powerful [[Limb/Legends|arms]], which terminated in hands with five fingers each. In contrast, their legs were relatively short; over all, the average member of the species stood 1.6 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall.<ref name="EGAS " /> Their heavy build afforded Ganks great strength,<ref name="TBS">''[[Galaxy of Fear: The Brain Spiders]]''</ref> yet they were also spry runners.<ref name="EA" /> They augmented their bodies with [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetics]],<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> making them a species of [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborgs]].<ref name="CSWE I 320">{{CSWECite|I|320|Gank}}</ref> These implants allowed Ganks to engage in silent communication with their fellows.<ref name="EGAS " />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|This is from Smada the Hutt. It's your turn to disappear.|A Gank Killer|<ref name="EA" />}}
[[File:Ganks.jpg|thumb|left|A pair of Gank Killers on Nar Shaddaa]]
Among members of other species, precious little was known about Gank culture well into the [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. The exception was that the Ganks were fabled for their violent and ruthless nature;<ref name="EGAS " /> even the slightest perceived insult was enough to throw a Gank into a violent rage of retaliation.<ref name="CN1:JT">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref> Outsiders similarly knew little of the organization of Gank society, or whether they had any central rulers at all. What was well known was that the Ganks were a war-loving and regimented species, whose members enjoyed occupations that allowed them to fight and shed [[Blood/Legends|blood]], such as that of [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]], [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]], [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], and [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]]. They were in particular demand by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], who had enough Ganks on retainer to constitute a small [[Army/Legends|army]].<ref name="EGAS " /> Their warlike ways and physical strength ranked the Ganks among [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] most redoubtable [[Soldier/Legends|fighters]].<ref name="POTJSB ">''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''</ref> The species had no compunctions about premeditated [[Death/Legends|murder]], which lent them the nickname "Gank Killers."<ref name="SWE ">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

Ganks rarely left any flesh exposed, so few non-Ganks had any idea what they truly looked like. They wore mechanized battle [[Armor/Legends|armor]] into combat. A typical suit consisted of cobbled-together pieces, such as a prolate spheroid-shaped helmet with small holes at the front and two thin poles emerging from each side. Other elements included [[Pauldron/Legends|pauldrons]], a chestplate, a belt, a loincloth, pants, a [[Holster/Legends|holster]], knee and elbow pads, [[Glove/Legends|gloves]], knee-high [[Boot/Legends|boots]], and small sheaths tied around the wrist to accommodate [[Knife/Legends|combat knives]]. From their necks some Ganks hung a variety of objects, including old [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]]. They otherwise had access to technology on par with the rest of [[Galactic community|galactic society]],<ref name="EGAS " /> such as [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblades]].<ref name="CN1:JT" />

Ganks rarely traveled alone;<ref name="EGAS " /> they preferred to work in packs to achieve their goals.<ref name="DEII 2">[[Dark Empire II 2|''Dark Empire II'' 2]]</ref> Although their society was divided into clans,<ref name="NEC ">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> they worked mostly in small groups of between two and five. Indeed, they worked so well together that [[sentientologist]]s hypothesized that Ganks possessed at least basic [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] abilities that allowed them to remain in constant communication with one another. However, no [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] was ever able to spend enough [[Time/Legends|time]] in close proximity to a group of Ganks to prove or even provide evidence for the theory. Ganks tended to kill any outsiders who approached them&mdash;including nosy anthropologists. An exception was the [[Senior Anthropologist]] and [[Shi'ido]] [[Changeling/Legends|shape-shifter]] [[Mammon Hoole]], who used his species' natural shape-shifting ability to infiltrate a pack of Ganks long enough to determine that they communicated through cybernetic implants, thus granting them an edge over other possible bodyguard candidates for the wealthy Hutts of [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]],<ref name="EGAS " /> a [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of the Hutt [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]].<ref name="CSWE II 361">{{CSWECite|II|361|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref>

Ganks [[Language/Legends|communicated verbally]] as well; some spoke [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]]. They also communicated through gestures and sounds, such as laughing when amused,<ref name="EA" /> shrieking when frightened, grunting when in pain,<ref name="EA" /> and screaming when injured severely.<ref name="CB ">{{JournalCite|14|Crimson Bounty}}</ref> A terrified Gank betrayed itself through the eyes.<ref name="EA" />

==History==
===Early history===
The Ganks' original [[Gank homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] was unknown to outsiders. However, at some point in their history, members of the species voyaged to Nar Shaddaa, which, over time, became their adopted home.<ref name="EGAS " /> There they took to working for the Hutts<ref name="SWTOR" /> as assassins, bodyguards, [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]], guards, and mercenaries. Their lust for blood, their affinity for working together as an effective team, and their ability to communicate with each other through mechanized means made Ganks prized assets of many a Hutt [[Gangster/Legends|gangster]],<ref name="EGAS " /> so Ganks were frequently seen on the moon as part of Hutt entourages.<ref name="CSWE I 320" />

The Ganks became infamous for their violent ways during the [[Gank Massacres]], which erupted in [[4800 BBY]]. At the time, [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]] discovered [[Ryll/Legends|ryll]] [[Spice/Legends|spice]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] and cornered the market in its distribution. The monopoly agitated the [[Porporite]] species, for whom ryll was highly addictive, sending them into homicidal rages upon its consumption. Neighboring factions,<ref name="NEC " /> including the Neimoidians themselves,<ref name="SWTOR" /> hired the Ganks for protection from the Porporites and to eliminate the threat they posed. The Gank clans committed [[Speciecide|genocide]] on the spice-addicted species, completely wiping them out.<ref name="NEC " /> Encouraged by their success,<ref name="SWTOR" /> the Ganks then embarked on a full scale war against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Their uprising was put down in [[4775 BBY]]<ref name="GAW ">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]<ref name="NEC " /> and their Republic allies after [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Vocatara]]<ref name="GAW " /> sent a force of [[juggernaut war droid]]s<ref name="NEGD ">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> and the [[Rocket-Jumper Elite Advance Unit]] to stop them.<ref name="GAW " /> The Neimoidians' use of Gank mercenaries rather than bounty hunters also constituted the first significant challenge to the dominance of the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]]. In response, some guild members took a page from the Ganks and worked for whomever paid the most, eventually fracturing the guild as more hard-line members quit in disgust.<ref name="BHC ">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref>

As early as [[3999 BBY]],<ref name="OTOTJ1">''[[Star Wars Omnibus: Tales of the Jedi Volume 1]]''</ref> the species had come to be known as "Gank Killers"<ref name="TOTJ 4" /> due to their penchant for killing other sentients without remorse.<ref name="CSWE I 320" /> During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], a period of unrest between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and the Galactic Republic, the word "gank" was used as an insult in general galactic parlance.<ref name="SWTOR" /> The species remained closely associated with the Hutts, although one group of Gank mercenaries moved into Imperial territory and geared up to pillage Empire-aligned planets. When the Sith Empire spotted them, they dispatched an operative to negotiate with the Ganks and persuade them to leave peacefully, thus avoiding hostilities between the Empire and the Hutts.<ref name="TOR D">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Diplomacy|Balancing Acts}}</ref> The name "Gank Killer" remained current into the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], when the [[Besalisk/Legends|Besalisk]] [[Restaurant/Legends|restauranteur]] [[Dexter Jettster/Legends|Dexter Jettster]] punned that the [[slider]]s he sold at his [[Dex's Diner/Legends|diner]] on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] had "no additives or Gank fillers."<ref name="DAD">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/dexdiner/index.html|text=Dining at Dex's|int=Dining at Dex's}}</ref>

By the latter [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the Galactic Republic, most Ganks lived in the lowest levels of Nar Shaddaa.<ref name="SWR 17">[[Star Wars (1998) 17|''Star Wars'' (1998) 17]]</ref> According to a legend that arose during the period and remained popular among Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]],<ref name="RGRCR ">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook]]''</ref> a group of fourteen Ganks once confronted the [[Korun/Legends|Korun]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]], surrounding him with [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] drawn.<ref name="POTJSB " /> Windu simply placed his hand on his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], looked each Gank in the eye, and said, "It's your decision." They dropped their weapons and turned themselves in to their would-be opponent.<ref name="RGRCR " /> Some Jedi thought the tale apocryphal, but it became an integral part of Windu's mystique among the members of his [[Jedi Order/Legends|order]].<ref name="NEGC ">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>

===Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|Hoole, you're a fool! Do you think a few frontier settlers are a match for my Ganks!|Smada the Hutt and his Gank forces face off against Mammon Hoole and Enzeen villagers|<ref name="EA" />}}
After the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Ganks remained an active threat in the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. In one instance in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] [[Journalist/Legends|journalist]] [[Den Dhur]] accidentally bumped into a group of three Ganks on the streets of Coruscant while stumbling home drunk from a [[Cantina/Legends|bar]]. [[Unidentified Gank thug 1|One]] backhanded him and knocked him over, while [[Unidentified Gank thug 2|another]] pulled a [[Vibroknife/Legends|vibroknife]] on the Sullustan's prone body in the gutter. Just before the Gank could cut him, the [[5YQ-series protocol droid|droid]] [[I-5YQ]] came to Dhur's aid. Upon hearing the [[Droid/Legends|droid's]] threat, the Ganks silently agreed to flee.<ref name="CN1:JT" />

[[File:Gank_EGAS.png|thumb|left|250px|A Gank wielding a blaster]]
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Ganks operated on several planets beyond [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]. For instance, the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] bounty hunter [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]] noted Ganks in the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley Cantina]] on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] when he visited that [[Water/Legends|watering]] hole with [[Spurch Goa]] and [[Dyyz Nataz]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="AHF:GT">{{StoryCite|story=A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> That same year, the [[Human/Legends|Human]] siblings [[Tash Arranda/Legends|Tash]] and [[Zak Arranda/Legends|Zak Arranda]] ran afoul of Ganks and their employer, [[Smada]] the Hutt, on the planet [[D'vouran]]. In an effort to pressure the Arandas' caretaker, Mammon Hoole, to assassinate a target for him, Smada had a [[Unidentified Gank minion 1|Gank thug]] assault Tash in the [[Don't Go Inn]] to underscore his message that Hoole must work for him. The timely intervention of the Human [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], and their companions convinced the Gank to release the girl and Smada to flee. Unperturbed, Smada used his Gank minions to accost the Aranda children again<ref name="EA" /> and again, eventually joining five Ganks on his [[Hoversled/Legends|hoversled]] to kill Zak and kidnap Tash, thus blackmailing Hoole into accepting Smada's offer of employment. Hoole arrived with twenty-four local villagers and convinced Smada to flee with his entourage. Smada continued his quest and sent a [[Unidentified Gank assassin|Gank assassin]] to shadow the children, who led the stalker to an abandoned [[Laboratory/Legends|laboratory]], where they were accompanied by a local man named [[Kevreb Bebo]], whom the Gank shot.<ref name="EA" /> The children fled, but Zak was captured and [[Prison/Legends|imprisoned]] in [[Smada's stronghold]] under guard by six Ganks. When Tash came to negotiate her brother's release, Smada and his Gank bodyguards were forced to take cover when they heard a [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragon]] roar&mdash;actually a trick by the [[Biological science droid|droid]] [[DV-9]], who came to the Arandas' rescue with the children's [[Skimboard/Legends|skimboard]]. The Ganks opened fire, but the children possessed<ref name="EA" /> a [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]] shaped like a pendant<ref name="CSWE I 66">{{CSWECite|I|66|Kevreb, Bebo}}</ref> that protected them from blasterfire. Seeing his Ganks unable to leap high enough to seize the children, Smada shot the board itself, and the children disappeared. Smada and six Ganks located the quarry outside, where the Hutt ordered [[Unidentified Gank minion 2|one Gank]] to capture the children. Instead, the Gank disappeared. The same fate befell the [[Unidentified Gank minion 3|next Gank]], who was swallowed up by the earth itself. The remaining five Ganks clambered aboard Smada's hoversled to avoid similar deaths, but the Hutt whipped all but [[Unidentified Gank minion 4|one]] off with his tail, and the ground swallowed them up. The [[Enzeen]] villager [[Chood]] appeared and explained that D'vouran itself was consuming the Ganks.<ref name="EA" /> When the Enzeen attacked, the remaining Gank leapt off the sled and ran for the [[Tree/Legends|forest]]. The planet ate the Gank.<ref name="EA" />

Two Ganks were hired by the Human [[Dominic Raynor]] to kill fellow Human [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] and his cyborg assistant, [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]], less than two [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after Calrissian became the [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]] of [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] on the planet [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]].<ref name="LCIA">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/fiction/f20080522/index.html|text="Lando Calrissian: Idiot's Array"|int=Lando Calrissian: Idiot's Array|newhost=Suvudu}}</ref> In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], a [[Unidentified Gank bounty hunter|Gank bounty hunter]] was hired by a Human counterpart named [[Thune (bounty hunter)|Thune]] to capture the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] smuggler [[Kaj Nedmak]]. The Gank loaded the [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]] in the back of a [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wing starfighter]] and flew it to a rendezvous with Thune, who had captured the Human smugglers [[Celia Durasha]] and [[Treytis Prash]] and stolen their [[Starship/Legends|ship]], the [[Starlight Red|''Faceted'']]. As Thune brought Durasha out to meet the Gank, Nedmak attempted to escape, but the Gank overpowered him, bringing him to the ''Faceted'' on Thune's order. However, as the Gank ascended the [[Entry ramp/Legends|gangway]], Nedmak fell to his knees and tripped the Gank, who fell down the ramp. In the confusion, Durasha and Nedmak overwhelmed Thune and took her captive. Nonetheless, the Gank bounty hunter recovered, shot Durasha's hand, and ordered the two to release Thune. Durasha then retrieved her blaster and shot and killed the Gank.<ref name="CB " />

Prior to the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the Hutt had Gank Killers in his employ. He sent some of them after Han Solo when the smuggler failed to pay back a debt he owed the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]]. Solo cited the Ganks chasing him as one reason why he had to abandon the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] to settle up with Jabba<ref name="ESBN" /> in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref name="NEC " /> Jabba enlisted Gank Killers to capture the [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police]] partners Spurch Goa and [[Thaffe]], as well as Dyyz Nataz, a smuggler traveling with them while the [[Detective/Legends|investigators]] pursued a counterfeit ring. Unbeknownst to them, Jabba had set the ring up specifically to entrap the investigators, who had annoyed him with their frequent arrests of his associates. The Ganks captured the trio, brought them onto an [[ore hauler]], and [[Torture/Legends|tortured]] Goa and Thaffe for [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] to gain intelligence for their employer. The pair refused to divulge any sensitive information, however, so the Ganks instead decided to kill the [[Police officer/Legends|police officers]]. They ordered the partners to play [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] against one another to determine who would die first. Thaffe lost on purpose, prompting the Ganks to shoot him. Goa went berserk and escaped, and Nataz freed himself in the ensuing chaos. The prisoners overpowered and killed the Ganks and then used the ship to make their escape.<ref name="DESB ">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>

===New Republic period and beyond===
[[File:GankSoloOrgana-DEII2.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Han and Leia Organa Solo are confronted by a gang of Gank Killers on Nar Shaddaa.]]
{{Quote|Shhh&hellip; Keep your voice down. It's Ganks! Those creeps work for the Hutts.|Han Solo, to Leia Organa Solo on Nar Shaddaa|<ref name="DEII 2" />}}
The Ganks maintained their mystique well after the rise of the New Republic due to their penchant for killing any researcher foolish enough to attempt to study them up close. One exception was the shape-shifting Shi'ido Senior Anthropologist Mammon Hoole, who managed to infiltrate a group of Gank Killers by changing his form to resemble theirs. Hoole had infringed on a Hutt's good graces, and the Hutt sent a group of Ganks after the scientist. Hoole turned a corner and assumed the form of his pursuers. When the group realized they had lost their target, they stopped to decide their next move. Hoole heard nothing, leading him to realize that the Ganks were able to maintain communication with one another through cybernetic implants. When they realized Hoole was an imposter, he transformed into a [[Rishii/Legends|Rishii]] [[Bird/Legends|avian]] and flew away. Hoole later included an entry on the Ganks in his [[Book/Legends|book]] ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', in which he recounted his discovery.<ref name="EGAS " />

Also in Hoole's book was a breakthrough in understanding Gank biology made by another researcher, [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Hira Deboota]] of the [[Coruscant State Coroner]]'s office. During the regime of the New Republic, Deboota noticed after performing an autopsy on a member of the cybernetic [[Yaka]] species that the Yaka's implants were similar to those of the Ganks, albeit slightly more advanced. Deboota hypothesized that Gank circuitry was a prototype for the final implementation of the devices used in the Yakas, a species whose cybernetic heritage came when the [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]] species experimented on them.<ref name="EGAS " />

On a trip to Nar Shaddaa in [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], a group of Ganks teamed up with the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] bounty hunter [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] to capture Han Solo and his [[Solo family/Legends|family]].<ref name="HB3">[[Star Wars Handbook 3: Dark Empire|''Star Wars Handbook'' 3: ''Dark Empire'']]</ref> Later that year, a group of Ganks working for the Hutts confronted Solo; his wife, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]]; and his former partner [[Salla Zend]] in Nar Shaddaa's [[Corellian Sector (Nar Shaddaa)/Legends|Corellian Sector]] while the trio of Humans attempted to find a starship to take them to the [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor's]] throneworld of [[Byss/Legends|Byss]] and to find the ancient Jedi [[Vima-Da-Boda]]. When the Ganks located the Solos, they demanded that the Humans surrender to the Hutts. Organa Solo unholstered her blaster and shot the pair of Ganks. When three more rushed to the scene, the Solos called their [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] partner, [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], to help. A rival gang of bounty hunters, also searching for the Solos, arrived and attacked the Gank Killers. In the fighting, the Ganks and bounty hunters wiped one another out, and their quarry escaped.<ref name="DEII 2" />

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], in [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]], at least two Ganks joined the group of [[Yuuzhan Vong]] sympathizers known as the [[Peace Brigade]]. When a group of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] reached the planet [[Ylesia/Legends|Ylesia]] and a [[Battle of Yag'Dhul (29 ABY)|battle]] broke out, the Ganks locked themselves in a bunker used by the [[Ylesian Senate]]. The [[New Jedi Order|Jedi]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] and [[Lowbacca]] infiltrated the bunker, and the Ganks opened fire. Lowbacca then bashed their heads together, ending the threat they posed.<ref name="Y">''[[The New Jedi Order: Ylesia]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I've got to pay off Jabba the Hutt or I'm a walking dead man ''[&hellip;]'' there will be too many [bounty hunters] to stop&hellip; Remotes, Gank killers, even Bell Cambos.|Han Solo explains his reasons for leaving Hoth in the second draft script for ''The Empire Strikes Back''|<ref name="MOESB ">''[[The Making of The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>}}
The Ganks date to the second draft of the script for [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], revised by [[George Lucas]] from the first draft by [[Leigh Brackett]] on [[April 1]], [[1978]]. In it, Han Solo tells Leia Organa that he must leave the Rebel Alliance's base on the ice planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] to pay off Jabba the Hutt. Organa protests, but Solo replies that if he fails to pay Jabba the [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|money]] he owes him, "there will be just too many [bounty hunters] to stop&hellip; Remotes, Gank killers, even Bell Cambos." The line was altered before shooting in [[1979]],<ref name="MOESB " /> and the reference to Gank killers removed.<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> Nevertheless, in his [[1980]] [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]] of the film, writer [[Donald F. Glut]] included a variant of the line, as did [[Archie Goodwin]] in his 1980 [[Star Wars (1977) 39|comic book adaptation]], thus preserving the reference.<ref name="ESBN" /> Solo's quote was repeated in ''[[The Empire Strikes Back Official Poster Monthly 5]]'', also published that year.<ref name="ESBOPM5 ">[[The Empire Strikes Back Official Poster Monthly 5|''The Empire Strikes Back'' Official Poster Monthly 5]]</ref>

Exactly what a "Gank killer" was remained unaddressed until issues [[Dark Empire 3|3]] and [[Dark Empire 4|4]] of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]'' were published by [[Dark Horse Comics]] in [[1991]] and [[1992]], respectively. The comics, written by [[Tom Veitch]] and illustrated by [[Cam Kennedy]], feature Hutt background characters with armored retainers. Although the comics never explicitly refer to these as Ganks, [[Bill Slavicsek]]'s [[1994]] [[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded|second edition]] and [[2000]] [[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Third Edition, Revised and Expanded|third edition]] of ''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]'' make such an identification.<ref name="AGTTSWU2 ">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref><ref name="AGTTSWU3 ">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Third Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> The species' background was expanded upon by [[Michael Allen Horne]] in [[1993]]'s ''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''<ref name="DESB " /> and by [[Ann Margaret Lewis (real person)|Ann Margaret Lewis]] in [[2001]]'s [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]. The latter source includes an image of the species by [[R. K. Post]].<ref name="EGAS " /> Ganks have since played minor roles in several ''[[Star Wars]]'' novels and stories, including [[John Whitman]]'s ''[[Galaxy of Fear: Eaten Alive]]'' ([[1997]]), [[Walter Jon Williams]]' "[[The New Jedi Order: Ylesia]]" ([[2002]]), and [[Michael Reaves]]' ''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]'' ([[2008]]).

Many sources, such as 1994's second edition of ''A Guide to the Star Wars Universe'', are unclear as to whether the terms ''Gank'' and ''Gank Killer'' refer to the same thing, or whether the Gank Killers were a subset of the Gank species as a whole.<ref name="AGTTSWU2 " /> However, 2000's third edition update to that book, also by Slavicsek, clarifies that the terms both refer to the species as a whole.<ref name="AGTTSWU3 " /> The species is also mentioned in sourcebooks such as the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'',<ref name="SWE " /> ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'',<ref name="CSWE I 320" /> and the [[codex]] of the [[2011]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''.<ref name="SWTOR" />

The unlicensed roleplaying magazine article "[[Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are]]" attributes the [[Gank system]] to [[Donald F. Glut]]'s ''[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]'' which was the first source to mention [[Gank/Legends|Gank killers]].<ref name="ESBN" />, and places the system in [[Spinward sector/Legends|Spinward sector]].<ref name="VSF13">{{VoyagesCite|13|Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are}}</ref>
